title: Hourly to Annual Pay: Use Our Salary Packaging Car Calculator for Better Planning
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our salary packaging car calculator. Understand tax, super, and state differences in ordinary-time earnings. Estimate your take-home
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equates to an annual gross salary of $52,261.44 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I use the hourly to annual calculator?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate. The calculator multiplies it by your weekly hours (default 38) and by 52 weeks to give an annual gross figure. If you are a casual employee, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top of the base rate. The result shows annual pay, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, and super. Remember that super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12%.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid to casual employees under the Fair Work Act. It compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. The calculator adds this loading on top of your base hourly rate when you select the checkbox. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated in this tool?
faqs.a: Superannuation is estimated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross salary. The calculator applies this rate up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes. This estimate does not include any salary sacrifice arrangements.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that gives an annual gross salary. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (set by the Fair Work Commission from 1 July 2026) produces an annual gross of $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44.

This calculator assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It uses the 2026–27 resident tax scale and the 2% Medicare levy (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Superannuation is added on top at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The result is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay or tax.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply double your weekly pay. For the minimum wage example, weekly pay is $1,004.90 (38 hours × $26.44), so fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing to salary offers expressed per fortnight.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has several pay rates that apply depending on your employment type and industry:

- **National Minimum Wage**: The base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific awards that set higher minimum wages, penalty rates, and allowances. Always check your relevant award through the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an additional 25% on top of the base rate (or award rate) to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the minimum wage, casuals earn $33.05 per hour.
- **Superannuation**: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay.

If you are a casual, use the checkbox on the calculator to add the 25% loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Ordinary-time earnings vary across states and territories due to differences in industry mix, cost of living, and award coverage. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) data. In May 2026, the national average for full-time adult ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week. However, this is a national average and does not represent a specific job or state. For example, mining and construction tend to pay above average, while retail and hospitality pay below. State-specific averages are available from the ABS, but this calculator uses the national average for reference. If you are comparing a job offer, consider the industry and location, and use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page to check award coverage.

### How Tax and Super Affect Your Take-Home Pay

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) withholds tax based on the 2026–27 resident tax brackets:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (unless you qualify for a reduction or exemption). The calculator estimates your tax and Medicare levy, but does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

Superannuation is separate: your employer adds 12% of your ordinary earnings to your super fund, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. This does not reduce your take-home pay directly, but it is a valuable part of your total compensation.

### Using the Salary Packaging Car Calculator

If you are considering salary packaging, such as a novated lease for a car, the net benefit depends on your tax bracket and the packaging arrangement. Our [salary packaging car calculator](/topics/super-and-packaging) helps you estimate how packaging affects your take-home pay and super contributions. For example, packaging a car can reduce your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax, but it also reduces your super guarantee base (since super is calculated on your reduced salary). The calculator accounts for these trade-offs. Remember that this tool does not include salary packaging deductions; you should use the dedicated calculator for that purpose.

### Practical Example: From Hourly to Annual

Let's say you are offered $35 per hour as a permanent full-time employee. Using 38 hours per week:

- Weekly gross: $35 × 38 = $1,330
- Fortnightly gross: $1,330 × 2 = $2,660
- Annual gross: $1,330 × 52 = $69,160
- Estimated tax (2026–27): approximately $11,367 (including Medicare)
- Estimated super (12%): $8,299.20 per year, paid on top
- Estimated take-home pay: about $57,793 per year

This is a simplified estimate. For a more precise calculation, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool and adjust for your specific circumstances.

### When to Use Award Rates Instead of Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is a safety net. Most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. If you know your award classification, use that rate instead of the minimum wage. The calculator works the same way: enter your award hourly rate and the calculator will apply the same formula.

### Important Disclaimer

This calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always consult a professional for your specific situation.

For more details on how your pay is calculated, visit our [reference tables](/data) or learn about [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).
